Adding a root-cause writeup for the variant that deduping `node_modules` doesn't fix, since that's what bit me and the `overrides`/reinstall advice earlier in #7415 sends you the wrong way for it.

The short of it: `<spinner>` only gets registered as a side effect of `import "opentui-spinner/solid"`, which runs `extend({ spinner })`. Once the build turned on `minify` (PR #22362), `bun build --compile` strips that import out of the executable as dead code, so the registration never runs and the reconciler throws on the first `<spinner>`. My `node_modules` had a single, correctly hoisted `@opentui/solid`, so reinstalling changed nothing.

I hit this on opencode `1.17.13` self-built from `dev`, Windows x64, bun `1.3.14` (the pinned version), with `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` at `0.3.4` and `opentui-spinner` at `0.0.7`, whose peer `^0.3.4` is satisfied so there's no second nested copy.

`opentui-spinner/dist/solid.mjs` calls `extend({ spinner: SpinnerRenderable })`, which writes `spinner` into `@opentui/solid`'s module-level component catalogue. The reconciler reads that same catalogue and throws `Unknown component type: spinner` when the key is missing. The one thing that triggers the write is the bare `import "opentui-spinner/solid"` with no bindings used, and with `minify: true` plus `splitting: true` (both from #22362) bun's dead-code elimination drops it. `opentui-spinner` does declare `sideEffects: ["./dist/solid.mjs"]`, so bun is arguably wrong not to honor it, but the practical result is that the registration is gone.

You can tell which variant you have without guessing. `cli-spinners` is imported only by `SpinnerRenderable`, which is referenced only by that registration, so its data surviving into the binary is a reliable signal:

```
grep -a -o bouncingBall "$(command -v opencode)"    # opencode.exe on Windows
```

On a crashing build that returns nothing (same for `dqpb`, `bouncingBar`, `toggle13`). After the code fix below they show up and the crash stops. Both builds had one `@opentui/solid@0.3.4` in `node_modules`, which is how you know it's lost at bundle time rather than an install problem.

**Config workaround, no rebuild.** Every `<spinner>` is guarded by the `animations_enabled` KV flag and falls back to a `⋯` text node. With opencode not running (it rewrites the file on exit), set it in the KV state file at `~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json` (the XDG state dir; the equivalent local-app-data path on Windows):

```json
{ "animations_enabled": false }
```

You can also flip it from the "Disable animations" command if the TUI stays up long enough. `opencode run` is unaffected either way (noted in #18590).

**Code fix that survives minify.** Make the import a binding that's actually used, so DCE can't prune it:

```ts
// packages/tui/src/component/spinner.tsx
// packages/tui/src/component/prompt/index.tsx

// import "opentui-spinner/solid"          // tree-shaken under minify
import { registerSpinner } from "opentui-spinner/solid"
registerSpinner()
```

`registerSpinner` is already exported by `opentui-spinner/solid`. It goes in the two TUI files that render a spinner. If `opencode run --mini` ever throws the same way, the same edit applies to `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/run/footer.view.tsx` and `footer.subagent.tsx`. Rebuild and the `cli-spinners` keys reappear.

The durable fix belongs upstream: either land that edit, or stop registering through a side-effect-only import and call `registerSpinner()` once at TUI startup where nothing can prune it. Probably worth a bun issue as well, since a subpath export listed in `sideEffects` shouldn't be dropped under `minify` + `splitting` + `--compile`.

This PR was closed by the automated stale cleanup, but the underlying workflow pain is still very real.

The change is intentionally small and already implemented: it adds a manual refresh action so the current WebUI workspace can reload its tools/config surfaces after MCP/config/skills/slash commands change.

This matters especially for people using the WebUI to create or iterate on skills. Without a refresh action, newly created or updated skills/commands often require restarting or working around the current running WebUI instance. I personally use the WebUI skill-creation flow frequently, so I currently have to maintain a self-built opencode just for this small missing capability.

This PR is not trying to introduce full hot reload or a watcher:
- no automatic file watching
- no session migration semantics
- no broad lifecycle changes
- no change to normal config update behavior

It is just a small manual refresh path for the current routed workspace/directory, with UI feedback.

If this exact shape is not preferred, I’d be happy to adjust the entry point, for example toward a `/reload` command, a different UI location, or a smaller backend primitive. But I believe the workflow itself is useful to many WebUI users, especially skill creators.
This is a MUST nowadays.

Upgraded to `1.17.13`.

I no longer see the `custom function name "bash" is reserved` error, but I don't think it's actually fixed — requests now fail earlier with a different error:

```
invalid request body: json: unknown field "summary"
```

Full log:
```
timestamp=2026-07-01T18:25:58.646Z level=ERROR run=f5550638 message="stream error" providerID=perplexity-agent modelID=google/gemini-3-flash-preview session.id=ses_0e111c070ffe3uzLdbNUeLv0pX small=true agent=title mode=primary error.error="AI_APICallError: invalid request body: json: unknown field \"summary\""
timestamp=2026-07-01T18:25:59.178Z level=ERROR run=f5550638 message="stream error" providerID=perplexity-agent modelID=anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 session.id=ses_0e111c070ffe3uzLdbNUeLv0pX small=false agent=build mode=primary error.error="AI_APICallError: invalid request body: json: unknown field \"summary\""
timestamp=2026-07-01T18:25:59.182Z level=ERROR run=f5550638 message=process session.id=ses_0e111c070ffe3uzLdbNUeLv0pX messageID=msg_f1eee3fb60016RVzf9nhM5ESRS error="invalid request body: json: unknown field \"summary\"" stack="AI_APICallError: invalid request body: json: unknown field \"summary\"\n    at <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bfez4scf.js:6:14583)\n    at async <anonymous> (/$bunfs/root/chunk-bfez4scf.js:6:12790)\n    at processTicksAndRejections (native:7:39)"
```

Affects both `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8` and `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` through the same `perplexity-agent` provider.

This coincides with #34702 (merged just before the `1.17.13` release), which makes opencode force a `reasoning.summary` field into requests for custom OpenAI-compatible providers like this one. That's a new field this gateway apparently doesn't accept, and its strict validation seems to reject the request before it would ever reach whatever check previously flagged `bash` as reserved. So this still looks like the same underlying incompatibility — just a different, earlier validation failure masking it now.

Based on the search results, here are the potentially related PRs:

   - Related because it deals with the `interleaved` field configuration for reasoning models, which is directly referenced in the current PR

   - Related because it addresses reasoning_content handling in message normalization

3. **PR #31599** - `refactor(provider): extract helpers from normalizeMessages`
   - Related because it refactors the same `normalizeMessages` function that this PR modifies

   - Related because it deals with reasoning parts handling

5. **PR #23501** - `fix: OpenAI-compatible provider improvements (system messages, image support, stream interruption)`
   - Related because it addresses OpenAI-compatible provider specific issues

These PRs are related to the same area (reasoning content handling and openai-compatible provider message normalization), though none appear to be exact duplicates of PR #34796. The most closely related is PR #24218 which deals with the `interleaved` configuration logic that this PR references.

this bites any server doing long-running work correctly per spec. Good analysis on the onprogress → progressToken chain — without the callback the token never gets injected, so resetTimeoutOnProgress: true is dead code exactly as you said.
For anyone blocked on this right now: I've been working around the whole class of problem by not holding the tool call open at all — return a job id immediately, stream progress through a separate watcher tool instead (https://github.com/arnavranjan005/mcp-telemetry). Doesn't excuse the client bug, but it sidesteps it, and works the same across opencode / Claude Code / Cursor since it doesn't depend on each host's timeout behavior.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #26762: Same root cause — `reasoning_content` in assistant message history rejected on follow-up turns by providers that don't support it (Cerebras)
- #25311: Same root cause — `reasoning_content` must/must-not be replayed in history depending on the provider; multi-turn failures with OpenAI-compatible providers
- #27852: Same root cause — 400 errors when `reasoning`/`reasoning_content` fields from prior turns are sent back in history to providers that reject them

The underlying issue (the AI SDK's `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` re-injecting `reasoning_content` into subsequent message history for providers that don't accept it) appears to be the same problem described in those issues, just observed with Ollama instead of Cerebras/DeepSeek/Kimi.

## Correction: the actual root cause is different

The `dbDir()` normalization in this PR is a minor safety net but **does not fix the reported issue**. The real root cause was found by inspecting the production DB on a real Windows installation.

### What the DB revealed

All 1052 sessions (from first use on May 24 to present) have:

| Column | Value |
|---|---|
| `directory` | `"C:/"` |
| `project_id` | `"global"` |
| `path` | `""` (empty) |

No session has ever been stored with a real workspace directory.

### Why this happens

**Storage side** — `ProjectV2.resolve()` at `packages/core/src/project.ts:111-112`:

```typescript
const repo = yield* git.repo.discover(input)
if (!repo) return { id: ID.global, directory: AbsolutePath.make(path.parse(input).root), vcs: undefined }
```

When no git repo is found (user works outside a git repo, or discovery fails), it returns the **drive root** (`C:/`) as the project directory. Sessions are then created via `InstanceStore.boot` which resolves the project context, and `ctx.directory` ends up as `C:/`. All sessions inherit this.

**Query side** — `V2Session.list()` at `packages/core/src/session.ts:276`:

```typescript
if ("directory" in input) conditions.push(eq(SessionTable.directory, dbDir(input.directory)))
```

The web app's `loadRootSessionsWithFallback` always passes the real working directory in the query. The DB has `"C:/"`, the query looks for `"C:/Users/<user>/..."` → **zero matches**.

### Why the backslash fix is insufficient

Drizzle's `directoryColumn.toDriver()` already normalizes `\` → `/` on both INSERT and WHERE. The `dbDir()` wrapper is redundant. The actual mismatch isn't `\` vs `/` — it's `"C:/"` (stored) vs `"C:/Users/..."` (queried). This is a directory **value** mismatch, not a format mismatch.

### Suggested proper fix

**Option A** — Change `ProjectV2.resolve()` to keep the original input directory when no git repo is found:

```typescript
if (!repo) return { id: ID.global, directory: input, vcs: undefined }
```

Sessions would then store the user's real working directory. `toDriver()` handles the normalisation to POSIX format on INSERT.

**Option B** — Skip directory filter for global-project sessions in `V2Session.list()`:

```typescript
if ("directory" in input && input.directory !== "C:/") {
  conditions.push(eq(SessionTable.directory, dbDir(input.directory)))
}
```

Or better, check against the project ID when available.

### This PR's status

The `dbDir()` changes are a harmless safety net but do not resolve #30374. The session-list-empty-on-restart bug will persist until the directory value mismatch above is addressed. I'll submit a follow-up with the correct fix once I can test it.
